sections.h2: Which Owen County offices handle a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices in Owenton touch an Owen County tax bill, and each has a separate job. The sheriff collects, the Property Valuation Administration (PVA) values the land, and the County Clerk holds delinquent bills and appeal paperwork.

Owen County offices for property tax (Owen County government pages)
OfficeRoleContact
SheriffCollects tax for the state, county and school districts103 W. Perry St., 502-484-3363, weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
Property Valuation AdministrationSets values; handles disputes about a bill502-484-5172
County ClerkDelinquent tax bills, deeds, liens136 W. Bryan St., 502-484-2213, weekdays 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed 12 to 1

The sheriff's page states that the office never assesses value, so any complaint about the amount goes to the PVA.

sections.h2: What is Owen County, Kentucky like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Owen County lies in northern Kentucky, with Owenton as the county seat and Glencoe and Gratz as the only other incorporated towns. It covers about 354 square miles, almost all of it land, and borders Carroll, Gallatin, Grant, Scott, Franklin and Henry counties. The legislature created it in 1819 from parts of Franklin, Scott, Gallatin and Pendleton counties, and it is named for Abraham Owen, a Kentucky legislator killed at the Battle of Tippecanoe.

The county is dry except for a winery and limited sales inside Owenton. Once the state built locks and dams on the Kentucky River, packet boats between Frankfort and Louisville began stopping at Gratz, Monterey and other river towns in the 1840s.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Owen County homes?
sections.html:
The numbers describe a small, owner-heavy market where the commute is long.

  • Population estimate for July 2025: 11,601, which is 3.0 percent above the 2020 base.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home (2020 to 2024): $168,700.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 88.0 percent among 4,252 households.
  • Median household income: $61,134; median gross rent: $830.
  • Mean travel time to work: 41.9 minutes, the longest among the four counties in the same Census comparison.
  • Households with a broadband subscription: 80.4 percent.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 17.

Employment data point the same way. The county had 133 employer establishments in 2023, and total employment slipped 1.5 percent from 2022.

sections.h2: When must Owen County owners pay, and what do late bills cost?
sections.html:
Kentucky uses one statutory schedule that the sheriff follows (KRS 134.015). A taxpayer who pays everything by November 1 gets a 2 percent discount. Anything paid November 2 through December 31 is billed at face value. January adds a 5 percent penalty, and from February the penalty becomes 10 percent.

The sheriff then keeps collecting until the close of business on April 15. After that, the unpaid bill is no longer a sheriff matter. It goes to the County Clerk as a certificate of delinquency, and the state's collection page says a lien is recorded on the property at that point.

sections.h2: How does an Owen County owner appeal an assessment?
sections.html:
The first move is a conference with the PVA. Under Kentucky's process, laid out in a PVA appeal guide, the owner states a value and supports it with sales of comparable houses, an appraisal, photos of damage or contractor estimates for repairs. Rental owners also bring income and expense records.

  1. Hold the PVA conference during the tax roll inspection period, which usually starts the first Monday in May.
  2. File the appeal form at the County Clerk's office on 136 W. Bryan Street by one business day after that period ends.
  3. Present evidence to the three-member local board of assessment appeals.
  4. If still unhappy, send a letter to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals within 30 days of the clerk's mailed ruling.

Owners who pay tax on their own claimed value during an appeal can face a supplemental bill if the final value is higher.

sections.h2: What happens to a delinquent Owen County bill?
sections.html:
The County Clerk's office keeps a list of delinquent property taxes, third party purchaser forms and a certificate of delinquency sale registration form on its website. For counties on the normal schedule, the Department of Revenue says a sale can be set between July 14 and August 28, at least 90 days after the bills reach the clerk.

  • Interest runs at 1 percent per month from the transfer.
  • The county attorney mails a 30-day notice and, if needed, a second notice that names the sale date.
  • The clerk advertises the list 30 to 45 days before the sale.
  • A private buyer who takes the certificate can then charge the owner additional fees.

Sellers should ask the Owen County Clerk at 502-484-2213 for a payoff before every closing on a parcel that appears on the list.

sections.h2: Which exemptions matter in Owen County?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption covers a primary residence owned by someone aged 65 or older, or by an owner who is totally disabled. It subtracts a set dollar amount from assessed value rather than exempting the home, and the amount is reset every two years. The exemption follows the owner, so a buyer files a new application. Totally disabled veterans with a service-connected rating do not have to reapply each year.

Farm acreage is valued at its agricultural use under Section 172A of the Kentucky Constitution. In a county as rural as Owen, that can cut an owner's taxable value sharply compared with market value, so the PVA is worth a call before a farm is sold or split.

sections.h2: What does an Owen County seller pay at closing?
sections.html:
The seller owes the state transfer tax, 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction, paid to the County Clerk when the deed is recorded (KRS 142.050). A sale at the $168,700 county median comes to 338 units and $169.00. Deeds between spouses, deeds that correct earlier deeds and deeds given only to secure a debt are exempt.

The deed also has to carry both parties' mailing addresses, the full price and an in-care-of address for the tax bill (KRS 382.135). A clerk may refuse a deed that leaves these out, which can delay a closing.

faqs.q: Who sets property values in Owen County?
faqs.a: The Owen County Property Valuation Administration sets them, and its number is 502-484-5172. The sheriff only collects the tax.

faqs.q: Where is the Owen County Sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: At 103 W. Perry St. in Owenton. It is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and the phone is 502-484-3363.

faqs.q: Is there an extra county tax on a sale in Owen County?
faqs.a: Kentucky's transfer tax applies statewide at 50 cents per $500 of value. On a $168,700 sale it comes to $169.00, and the seller pays it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: What if my Owen County tax bill is already delinquent?
faqs.a: Contact the County Clerk at 502-484-2213. After April 15 the bill sits there as a certificate of delinquency with a recorded lien, and interest of 1 percent per month applies.

faqs.q: Can I get a homestead exemption in Owen County at age 65?
faqs.a: Yes, if the house is your permanent residence. File the application with the PVA, and a buyer of your house will need to file a new one.
